summary: 茶从中国经荷兰商人进入欧洲后，逐渐成为英国咖啡馆与家庭的饮品。英国的茶税、走私、东印度公司垄断及其终结，又陆续改变了合法茶价、供货地和海运竞争。
logic: 中国茶文化及日本传播
荷兰贸易将茶带入欧洲
英国高茶税催生走私与掺假
贸易开放改变产地及运茶航线

paragraphs.brief: 神农传说与中国饮茶史料
sentences: The story of tea begins in China.
茶的故事从中国开始
According to legend, in 2737 BC the Chinese emperor Shen Nung was sitting beneath a tree while his servant boiled drinking water, when some leaves from the tree blew into the water.
传说公元前2737年，神农坐在树下，仆人正在烧水，几片树叶被风吹进水中。
Shen Nung, a renowned herbalist, decided to try the infusion that his servant had accidentally created.
神农通晓草药，决定尝尝仆人意外泡出的这杯水。
The tree was a Camellia sinensis, and the resulting drink was what we now call tea.
那棵树是茶树（Camellia sinensis），泡出的饮品就是今天所说的茶。
It is impossible to know whether there is any truth in this story, but tea-drinking certainly became established in China many centuries before it had even been heard of in the West.
这种故事是否有任何真理是不可能知道的，但茶饮确实在西方人听到之前，在中国建立了许多世纪。

Containers for tea have been found in tombs dating from the Han Dynasty (206 BC–220 AD), but it was under the Tang Dynasty (618–906 AD) that tea became firmly established as the national drink of China.
在汉王朝(206 BC-220 AD)的墓穴中发现了茶叶容器，但茶叶在唐王朝(618-906 AD)下牢固地成为中国的民族饮料。
paragraphs.gist: 神农尝茶的传说已难考证，但汉墓出土的茶具说明中国很早便有饮茶习惯，到了唐代，茶更确立了全国性饮品的地位。

paragraphs.brief: 陆羽著书与茶传入日本
sentences: It became such a favourite that during the late eighth century a writer called Lu Yu wrote the first book entirely about tea, the Ch’a Ching, or Tea Classic.
茶广受喜爱，以至于八世纪末陆羽写下第一部专门讲茶的著作《茶经》。
It was shortly after this that tea was first introduced to Japan, by Japanese Buddhist monks who had travelled to China to study.
不久之后，赴中国求学的日本僧人首次将茶传入日本。
Tea received almost instant imperial sponsorship and spread rapidly from the royal court and monasteries to the other sections of Japanese society.
茶叶几乎很快得到帝国赞助，从皇宫和寺院迅速蔓延到日本社会的其他阶层。
paragraphs.gist: 八世纪末陆羽写下首部茶学专著《茶经》，不久赴华求学的日本僧人将茶带回，在皇室支持下从宫廷寺院传播到日本其他阶层。

paragraphs.brief: 欧洲人最早的饮茶记载
sentences: So at this stage in the history of tea, Europe was rather lagging behind.
所以在茶叶史的这个阶段，欧洲相当落后。
In the latter half of the sixteenth century there are the first brief mentions of tea as a drink among Europeans, mostly from Portuguese who were living in the East as traders and missionaries.
直到十六世纪后半叶，欧洲人才首次简短记载茶这种饮品，记录多来自旅居东方的葡萄牙商人和传教士。
But although some of these individuals may have brought back samples of tea to their native country, it was not the Portuguese who were the first to ship back tea as a commercial import.
虽然其中一些人可能已经把茶样品带回了自己的祖国，但不是葡萄牙人首先把茶作为商业进口运回。
paragraphs.gist: 十六世纪后半叶欧洲才零星提到饮茶，记录多出自旅居东方的葡萄牙商人和传教士，但最先把茶作为商业进口货运回的另有其人。

paragraphs.brief: 荷兰开拓欧洲商业茶叶进口
sentences: This was done by the Dutch, who in the last years of the sixteenth century began to encroach on Portuguese trading routes in the East.
最先这样做的是荷兰人；十六世纪末，他们开始进入葡萄牙人在东方经营的贸易航线。
By the turn of the century they had established a trading post on the island of Java, and it was via Java that in 1606 the first consignment of tea was shipped from China to Holland.
到了本世纪之交，他们在爪哇岛建立了一个贸易站，1606年，第一批茶叶从中国运到荷兰。
Tea soon became a fashionable drink among the Dutch, and from there spread to other countries in continental western Europe, but because of its high price it remained a drink for the wealthy.
茶叶很快成为荷兰人中时髦的饮料，从那里蔓延到西欧大陆的其他国家，但由于茶叶价格高昂，它仍然是富人的一种饮料。
paragraphs.gist: 荷兰商人经爪哇在 1606 年把首批中国茶运回荷兰，饮茶风尚随后传入西欧其他地区，却因价格昂贵而主要限于富人。

sentences: Britain, always a little suspicious of continental trends, had yet to become the nation of tea-drinkers that it is today.
英国历来对欧洲大陆的时尚略抱怀疑，当时还没成为今日这个爱喝茶的国家。
Starting in 1600, the British East India Company had a monopoly on importing goods from outside Europe, and it is likely that sailors on these ships brought tea home as gifts.
从1600年开始，英国东印度公司垄断从欧洲以外进口货物，这些船上的水手很可能把茶作为礼物带回家。
The first coffee-house had been established in London in 1652, and tea was still somewhat unfamiliar to most readers, so it is fair to assume that the drink was still something of a curiosity.
伦敦首家咖啡馆开于1652年，茶对多数读者仍相当陌生，因此不难推断它那时还算新奇饮品。
paragraphs.gist: 十七世纪初英国东印度公司垄断从欧洲以外地区进口商品，海员可能把茶当礼物带回，但到伦敦首家咖啡馆出现时，多数人仍对茶陌生。

paragraphs.brief: 英国咖啡馆饮茶的阶层与性别差异
sentences: Gradually, it became a popular drink in coffee-houses, which were as much locations for the transaction of business as they were for relaxation or pleasure.
逐渐地，它成为咖啡馆的热门饮料，咖啡馆与放松或娱乐一样是交易场所。
They were, though, the preserve of middle- and upper-class men; women drank tea in their own homes, and as yet tea was still too expensive to be widespread among the working classes.
不过，咖啡馆是中上层男性的天地，女性在家饮茶；茶价仍高，工人阶层尚难普遍享用。
In part, its high price was due to a punitive system of taxation.
其高价部分是由于惩罚性税收制度。
paragraphs.gist: 茶渐成兼做生意与休闲场所的咖啡馆里的热门饮品，但那里主要接待中上层男性，女性在家饮茶，而重税使工人阶层仍难负担。

paragraphs.brief: 高额茶税催生有组织的走私
sentences: One unforeseen consequence of the taxation of tea was the growth of methods to avoid taxation—smuggling and adulteration.
征收茶税产生了一个意外后果：走私与掺假等避税手段日益盛行。
By the eighteenth century many Britons wanted to drink tea but could not afford the high prices, and their enthusiasm for the drink was matched by the enthusiasm of criminal gangs to smuggle it in.
到了十八世纪，许多英国人想喝茶，却承担不起高价；他们有多热衷饮茶，犯罪团伙就有多热衷走私。

What began as a small-time illegal trade, selling a few pounds of tea to personal contacts, developed by the late eighteenth century into an astonishing organised-crime network, perhaps importing as much as seven million lb annually, compared to a legal import of five million lb!
起初是小规模的非法贸易，出售几磅茶给个人接触，发展成惊人的有组织犯罪网络，可能每年进口700万磅，而合法进口500万磅!
paragraphs.gist: 重税催生走私与掺假，小规模私下买卖最终变成犯罪网络，到十八世纪末，每年走私的茶甚至可能超过合法进口量。

sentences: Worse for the drinkers was that taxation also encouraged the adulteration of tea, particularly of smuggled tea which was not quality-controlled through customs and excise.
更糟糕的是，税收也鼓励了茶叶的掺假，特别是走私茶叶，而走私茶叶不是通过关税和消费税进行质量控制的。
Leaves from other plants, or leaves which had already been brewed and then dried, were added to tea leaves.
其他植物的叶子，或已经煮好、然后干燥的叶子被添加到茶叶上。
By 1784, the government realised that enough was enough, and that heavy taxation was creating more problems than it was worth.
到1784年，政府意识到不能再这样下去，重税造成的问题已超过它能带来的好处。
The new Prime Minister, William Pitt the Younger, slashed the tax from 119 per cent to 12.5 per cent.
新任首相小威廉·皮特把税率从119%大幅降至12.5%。
Suddenly legal tea was affordable, and smuggling stopped virtually overnight.
突然，合法茶可以买得起，走私活动几乎一夜之间停止。
paragraphs.gist: 走私茶缺少检验，常被掺入其他叶子或泡过再烘干的茶叶；1784 年小皮特大幅减税后，合法茶价下降，走私几乎一夜间停息。

paragraphs.brief: 印度茶园发展改变英国进口来源
sentences: Another great impetus to tea-drinking resulted from the end of the East India Company’s monopoly on trade with China, in 1834.
茶叶饮料的另一个巨大推动力是1834年东印度公司结束对中国贸易的垄断。

Before that date, China was the country of origin of the vast majority of the tea imported to Britain, but the end of its monopoly stimulated the East India Company to consider growing tea outside China.
在此之前，中国是进口给英国的绝大多数茶叶的来源国，但垄断的结束促使东印度公司考虑在中国以外种植茶叶。
India had always been the centre of the Company’s operations, which led to the increased cultivation of tea in India, beginning in Assam.
印度一直是该公司业务的中心，这导致印度从阿萨姆开始种植更多的茶叶。

There were a few false starts, including the destruction by cattle of one of the earliest tea nurseries, but by 1888 British tea imports from India were for the first time greater than those from China.
起初经历了几次挫折，例如早期一处茶树苗圃被牛群毁坏；但到1888年，英国从印度进口的茶首次超过从中国进口的数量。
paragraphs.gist: 东印度公司对华贸易垄断结束后转向印度种茶，尽管早期茶圃曾遭牛群破坏，1888 年英国从印度进口的茶终于首次超过中国。

paragraphs.brief: 贸易开放开启运茶快帆船时代
sentences: The end of the East India Company’s monopoly on trade with China also had another result, which was more dramatic though less important in the long term: it ushered in the era of the tea clippers.
东印度公司对华贸易垄断的结束，还有一个更为戏剧性但长期意义较小的结果：它开启了快速运茶帆船的时代。
While the Company had had the monopoly on trade, there was no rush to bring the tea from China to Britain, but after 1834 the tea trade became a virtual free-for-all.
公司垄断贸易时，运茶从中国回英国无须争分夺秒；1834年以后，茶叶贸易却几乎成了人人都能加入的自由竞争。
paragraphs.gist: 垄断时期运茶无需争快，1834 年贸易放开后商人纷纷竞争，把茶尽早运回英国的需要由此开启了快速运茶帆船的时代。

paragraphs.brief: 英美运茶竞赛与蒸汽航运兴起
sentences: Individual merchants and sea-captains with their own ships raced to bring home the tea and make the most money, using fast new clippers which had sleek lines, tall masts and huge sails.
独立商人和拥有船只的船长驾驶船身流畅、桅杆高耸、风帆巨大的新式快帆船，竞相把茶抢先运回以赚取最多利润。
In particular, there was competition between British and American merchants, leading to the famous clipper races of the 1860s.
竞争尤以英美商人之间最为激烈，催生了十九世纪六十年代著名的运茶快帆船竞速。
But these races soon came to an end with the opening of the Suez Canal, which made the trade routes to China viable for steamships for the first time.
但随着苏伊士运河的开通，这些赛事很快就结束了，这第一次使通往中国的贸易路线成为了蒸汽船的可行路线。
paragraphs.gist: 英美商人用高桅大帆的快船竞相运茶，十九世纪六十年代的竞速尤其著名；苏伊士运河通航后轮船也能经济地走这条航线，竞赛随之结束。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: Tea was popular in Britain in the 16th century.
items.zh: 16 世纪，茶在英国很受欢迎。
items.why: 到十七世纪中期，多数英国读者尚不熟悉茶，说明茶在十六世纪并未在英国普及。

items.en: Tea was more fashionable than coffee in Europe in the late 16th century.
items.zh: 16 世纪末，在欧洲喝茶比喝咖啡更时髦。
items.why: 文中说十六世纪后半叶欧洲人开始简短提及饮茶，没有与当时咖啡的流行程度作比较。

items.en: Tea was enjoyed by all classes in Britain in the 17th century.
items.zh: 17 世纪，英国各个社会阶层的人都喝茶。
items.why: 茶价对劳动阶层仍太高，当时常见的消费者主要属中上阶层，并非各阶层都享用。

items.en: The adulteration of tea also prompted William Pitt the Younger to reduce the tax.
items.zh: 茶叶掺假也是促使小威廉·皮特降低茶税的原因之一。
items.why: 高税不只刺激走私，还助长掺假；这也是政府后来大幅降低茶税的背景。

items.en: Initial problems occurred when tea was planted outside China by the East India Company.
items.zh: 东印度公司在中国以外种植茶树时，起初遇到了困难。
items.why: 早期试种曾多次受挫，包括一处茶苗圃遭牛破坏，可见初期确有问题。

items.en: The fastest vessels were owned by America during the 19th-century clipper races.
items.zh: 在 19 世纪的飞剪船竞速中，最快的船只属于美国。
items.why: P10 仅说英美“competition…famous clipper races”。未说明最快船只归美国上所有，信息不足。

points: 到十七世纪中期，多数英国读者尚不熟悉茶，说明茶在十六世纪并未在英国普及。
回到对应内容“最先这样做的是荷兰人；十六世纪末，他们开始进入葡萄牙人在东方经营的贸易航线”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: According to legend, in 2737 BC the Chinese emperor Shen Nung was sitting beneath a tree ….
连接词 while 引出“while his servant boiled drinking water, when some leaves from the tree blew into the water”，说明主句的时间或对比关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 while 把这一层关系补进去。
It is impossible to know …, but tea-drinking certainly became established in China many centuries before it had even been heard of in the West.
“whether there is any truth in this story”补足 know 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 know 所在的主句，再把 whether 后面的内容作为一个整体。
